text:
maria: follow-up: i prototyped a small sandbox for Orbit that nails two things: (1) tenant isolation for prefetch budgets, (2) reproducible decision traces for audits. want feedback on the enforcement surface before we wire it into runtime.
kevin: nice. what does "sandbox" mean here? process boundary? cgroup?
maria: two-mode approach: a runtime in-proc mode (fast, quantized net) and a strict sandboxed worker process mode (isolated cgroup, capped io/cpu) we can enable per-cluster. default = in-proc for latency-sensitive canaries.
yara: sounds sensible. for per-tenant limits we need clear knobs. propose: tenant_prefetch_budget = absolute_pages and tenant_prefetch_pct (of tenant_quota). enforcement points: (a) scheduler respects budget when emitting hints, (b) residency manager rejects prefetch pins above budget.
dmitri: prefer enforcement in residency manager (single source of truth). scheduler can be honest or pessimistic; residency manager performs hard clamp. avoids race conditions if scheduler misbehaves.
anita: small ops concern: if residency manager hard rejects, we should surface a structured reason code to the scheduler so it can downgrade decisions (defer vs partial prefetch). otherwise opaque failures will be confusing in traces.
maria: agreed. new API shape: ResidencyManager.try_pin(tenant_id, pages:list) -> {ok: bool, pinned: int, reason: "quota|pressure|error"}. scheduler adapts.
kevin: we should not add nested objects in the wire; keep it small: try_pin returns a short enum + int. e.g., "ok, pinned=3, reason=quota" — simple text.
yara: logging/traceability: each decision should attach a decision_id and causal chain: request_id -> decision_id -> try_pin_result. Add debug sampling flag to avoid trace blowup.
dmitri: fairness enforcement: what if one tenant abuses the prefetch cap by issuing many tiny requests that together saturate bandwidth? quotas must be enforced on a rolling window (pages/sec) and also burst cap (pages per request).
maria: propose parameters: tenant.burst_pages_max, tenant.rate_pages_per_sec, tenant.prefetch_pool_pct. Defaults: burst=8, rate=20/sec, pool_pct=0.12. Also global emergency cap if aggregate prefetch_pct across tenants > 0.6 then reduce all non-critical prefetching.
kevin: emergency cap needs deterministic tie-breakers. maybe prioritize by SLA tier, then by recent hit-rate. don't want noisy tenants killing premium customers.
anita: add customer opt-out toggle (console) and also a per-workload opt-out tag. legal/reg customers can opt-out of predictive prefetch entirely.
ymaria-note: (ops-bot) deploy: bench job queued: orbit-sandbox-smoke.
bench-bot: bench-bot: smoke run started on canary pool id=orbit-canary-7. logs -> /bench/7471111222-orbit-smoke.log
yara: observability: metrics we need: orbit.sandbox.cpu_ms, orbit.sandbox.io_mb, orbit.rejects_by_reason, orbit.prefetch.success_ratio_by_tenant, orbit.prefetch.bytes_by_tenant, orbit.decision.trace_sample_count.
dmitri: also instrument cost attribution: orbit.prefetch.egress_cost and orbit.prefetch.device_time_ms so biz can see GPU-hour delta.
maria: training/validation note: we MUST include negative examples in sim (noise tenants, request storms). offline reward = baseline_p99_improvement - alpha * bandwidth_cost - beta * fairness_violation_score. tune alpha/beta conservatively.
kevin: ops question: model updates. if we update RL weights, how do we ensure no MLOps surprise? answer: versioned models, warmed in staging, shadow-run for X hours, then gradual rollout. if model fails, fallback to deterministic heuristic.
yara: debugging UX: add a "decision explain" endpoint that returns top-k reasons (features) the model used. keep it stripped of any PII. helps SRE debugging.
anita: security: model/decision traces must be scrubbed for customer data. policy: only include page identifiers (abstract ids) and counts, no raw prompt content.
dmitri: can we precompute a small policy table for tiny models? gives fully deterministic fallback with similar footprint. good for customers wanting provable behavior.
maria: yes. fallback ladder: 1) RL in-proc, 2) quantized policy-table, 3) heuristic predictor. We can pin customers to a rung.
kevin: rollout plan: feature-flagged canary pool -> gather metrics for 48h -> compare P99, bandwidth, prefetch_miss_rate -> then slow rollout 10/30/60% -> full. Add hard global kill switch.
yara: tests: unit tests for try_pin semantics, integration test with residency manager, chaos test where residency manager rejects 50% of pins, and e2e bench to confirm no regression on median latency.
anita: ops playbook snippets: how to disable Orbit on a node, how to revoke all prefetch pins, and how to audit decisions for a customer. keep them in runbook repo.
maria: any objections to the placement decision (hints-only + enforcement in residency manager)?
dmitri: none from me. keeps residency decisions atomic.
kevin: none, but insist on clear tracing and error enums.
yara: lgtm. i'll draft the telemetry PR and dashboard layout.
maria: i'll write RFC draft w/ config defaults + canary plan + sim results after bench completes.
anita: i'll add runbook stubs and console toggle UX.
ops-bot: (ops-bot) note saved: orbit-sandbox-fairness-thread archived.
maria: thanks all — leaving thread to collect any late concerns. :rocket:
